role: Secondary interpretation and cross-checks. The preserved published novel remains the source for mapped geography.

references.title: Mapping the Text of Lilith: MacDonald’s Labyrinths and Gardens
references.author: Kaitlyn Dryer

references.title: Lilith by MacDonald Study Guide
references.author: Dale J. Nelson
references.publication: Study notes copyright 2000, posted on SFF Chronicles in January 2012
references.kind: Study guide and interpretation of the published novel
references.edition: Page references use the 1994 reprint of the 1981 Eerdmans edition, not our Gutenberg paragraph locators.
relevance: Notes 29, 55, and 117 discuss how moral and spiritual states affect perception. Useful for later changes in scene appearance.
Note 61 contrasts Lilith’s enclosed palace with Mara’s open doors and unglazed windows. Useful for architectural atmosphere.
Note 117 discusses Dante parallels while treating purgatory primarily as suffering and learning. This does not establish another mapped territory.

references.title: The Spiritual Structure of Lilith
references.author: Greville MacDonald, with introduction and notes by John Docherty
references.kind: Paraphrase of the first manuscript draft, with quotations, interpretation, and critical notes
relevance: Interprets the hot stream through its warmth, metallic taste, water, and rising mist. Useful visual cues; symbolic interpretation does not establish a physical link to the great river.
Compares earlier and published versions of the ivy hall, Bulika, restoration, and the final mountain city. Version differences must stay explicit.
Docherty’s notes challenge several assertions in Greville’s account, including the identity of the hand-burier and aspects of symbolic interpretation.

published_text_cross_check.46.024: The published text describes river steps of porphyry and serpentine, with shallower walking steps on both banks. The manuscript paraphrase instead describes malachite and porphyry stairs across house tops; those details should not replace the published scene.
